| Scene description | • S04-B covers building surroundings and planting edges at Qunguang Plaza, Hongshan District.<br>• S04-B-01: transparent sheeting covers a construction or storage area with cardboard, bags, foam packaging, and small black waste particles beside two red extinguishers.<br>• S04-B-02: two green food-waste bins against an old wall are visibly stained, with woven sacks, board fragments, discarded paint cans, and foam food containers around them.<br>• S04-B-03: partly damaged black bags lie near a manhole beside overgrown planting, surrounded by leaves and minor litter. No sorting bins visibly overflow, but multiple accumulations mix construction, packaging, and municipal waste. |
| Regulatory basis | • Commercial public-space managers or operators should provide standard containers and adequate sanitation facilities. Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 44, [D-06-C010](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Indiscriminate dumping, scattering, or stockpiling requires cessation and correction within a deadline, with CNY 5,000–50,000 for organizations or up to CNY 200 for individuals. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 42, [D-03-C007](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Stockpiling, stalls, or unauthorized promotional displays in roads, squares, and public places breach appearance rules and are subject to enforcement. Wuhan Municipal Regulations on Integrated Urban Management, Article 63, [D-07-C011](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Commercial areas fall within public places covered by the Guidelines; managers should implement source reduction, sorting, and collection, with unlisted settings following comparable functions. Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings, Section 1.2. Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings, Section 1.2, [D-16-C001](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv).<br>• Operators of airports, malls, stadiums, and other public facilities should provide collection facilities under national sanitation requirements. Ecological and Environmental Code of the People’s Republic of China, Article 510, paragraph 1, [D-01-C003](../../../data/knowledge_base/clause_catalog.csv). |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Four accumulations mix construction, packaging, and municipal waste at planting edges and public areas, impairing appearance and posing sanitation risks without severe pollution or public safety threats. No bins overflow. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts include poorer sanitation, obstructed pedestrian access and scenery, small fragments escaping damaged bags, and possible insects or odors. Possible short-term impacts include complaints from businesses or residents and rainfall dispersal into planting or drainage. |
| Potential causes | - **Possible cause 1:** businesses or contractors leave temporary waste without prompt removal; sheeting, packaging, cardboard, foam, and extinguishers at S04-B-01 support this.<br>- **Possible cause 2:** insufficient bins or delayed collection, suggested by materials around stained bins at S04-B-02.<br>- **Possible cause 3:** weak sorting guidance or unclear management responsibility; unlabeled bags lie by a manhole at S04-B-03.<br>- **Verification:** identify responsible sorting managers and review collection records, bin provision, and collection frequency. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, sanitation may deteriorate, breeding insects and rodents and increasing transmission risks; urban appearance and business or customer satisfaction may decline; repeated penalties may raise management costs; and waste entering soil or water may cause pollution. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** clear S04-B-01, S04-B-02, and S04-B-03, separately removing construction and municipal waste; wash and disinfect bin surroundings; provide temporary construction barriers and signs with responsible organizations and removal deadlines.<br>- **Long-term measures:** Qunguang Plaza managers should provide marked sorting bins and locations under the Wuhan Guidelines for Municipal Solid Waste Classification in Major Settings; log collections and ensure daily removal; train businesses and contractors in sorting and sanitation duties; inspect, stop, and record improper storage. |
| Priority | **Medium.** Multiple accumulations affect appearance and public sanitation and may recur despite no severe pollution or safety threat. Prompt removal and durable management are needed to prevent escalation. |
